verses.text: Joshua gathered all Israel's tribes at Shechem. He called the elders, leaders, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God.
Joshua told everyone, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘Long ago your ancestors lived across the Euphrates, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor. They served other gods.
I took your ancestor Abraham from across the river, led him through all of Canaan, and gave him many descendants. I gave him Isaac.
I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau Mount Seir as his own, while Jacob and his children went down to Egypt.
I sent Moses and Aaron, struck Egypt with plagues, and then brought you out.
I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians chased your ancestors to the Red Sea with chariots and horsemen.

When your ancestors cried out to the LORD, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. You saw for yourselves what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness a long time.
I brought you into the land of the Amorites across the Jordan. They fought you, and I handed them over to you. You took their land, and I destroyed them ahead of you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, rose up to fight Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
I refused to listen to Balaam, so he kept blessing you, and I rescued you from his hand.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought you, along with the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites. I handed them over to you.
I sent the hornet ahead of you to drive them out, including the two Amorite kings. It didn't take your sword or your bow.
I gave you land you hadn't worked and towns you hadn't built. You live in them now, and you eat from vineyards and olive groves you never planted.’
So honor the LORD and serve him sincerely and faithfully. Get rid of the gods your ancestors served across the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

If serving the LORD seems wrong to you, choose today whom you'll serve. Will it be the gods your ancestors served across the river or the gods of the Amorites whose land you live in? As for me and my household, we'll serve the LORD.”
The people answered, “We would never abandon the LORD to serve other gods!

The LORD our God brought us and our ancestors out of slavery in Egypt. He did those great signs right before our eyes and protected us along the whole journey and among all the peoples we passed through.
The LORD drove out all those peoples ahead of us, including the Amorites who lived here. So we'll serve the LORD too, because he's our God.”
Joshua told the people, “You can't serve the LORD, because he's a holy God and a jealous God. He won't forgive your rebellion and sins.
If you abandon the LORD and serve foreign gods, he'll turn against you, bring disaster on you, and destroy you after all the good he's done for you.”
The people answered Joshua, “No, we will serve the LORD.”
Joshua said, “You're witnesses against yourselves that you chose the LORD for yourselves and chose to serve him.” They answered, “We are witnesses.”
“Then get rid of the foreign gods among you and turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
The people told Joshua, “We'll serve the LORD our God and listen to his voice.”
That day Joshua made a covenant with the people at Shechem and gave them a law and a ruling to live by.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up under the oak by the LORD's sanctuary.
Joshua told everyone, “Look at this stone. It'll be a witness against us because it heard everything the LORD said to us. It'll testify against you if you deny your God.”
Then Joshua sent everyone home to their own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the LORD's servant, died at 110 years old.
They buried him within his own land at Timnathserah in Ephraim's hill country, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD throughout Joshua's life and throughout the lives of the elders who outlived him and knew everything the LORD had done for Israel.

The Israelites buried Joseph's bones, which they'd brought out of Egypt, at Shechem, in the plot Jacob had bought for a hundred pieces of silver from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem. That plot became the inheritance of Joseph's descendants.
Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him on the hill belonging to his son Phinehas, which had been given to him in Ephraim's hill country.
